title: Amanda Batula Fires Back as Ex Kyle Cooke Pops Up in Boyfriend West Wilson’s Instagram Comments
body:
Summer House alumna Amanda Batula has publicly responded to a heated Instagram exchange in which her estranged husband, Kyle Cooke, launched a personal attack on her new boyfriend, West Wilson. Cooke’s scathing comment, in which he labeled Wilson a “coke head,” sparked a flurry of speculation across social‑media platforms about the couple’s turbulent dynamics and the future of Batula’s involvement in Bravo’s spin‑off series In the City. In a measured statement posted to her own Instagram story, Batula defended Wilson, dismissed Cooke’s remarks as “unnecessary drama,” and hinted that she is focusing on her own well‑being rather than the ongoing feud.

The exchange unfolded after Cooke, who shares a child with Batula, posted a series of Instagram comments on Wilson’s recent photo, accusing the 31‑year‑old model‑turned‑entrepreneur of substance abuse. Cookes’s remarks quickly went viral, prompting fans of the reality franchise to weigh in on the alleged “coke head” claim. Many users expressed concern for Wilson, while others rallied behind Batula, urging the former Summer House cast member to “keep her head up” and “stay out of the drama.” The online backlash against Cooke was swift, with several accounts calling for him to seek professional help rather than airing personal grievances publicly.

Batula’s response, though brief, was notable for its composure. In a story that lasted the platform’s full 15 seconds, she wrote, “I’m not here for the drama. West is a kind, caring person and I love him. Let’s keep the focus on positivity.” The post was accompanied by a photo of the couple smiling together at a recent charity event, underscoring the pair’s desire to project a united front. By framing the narrative around love and positivity, Batula appears to be steering the conversation away from the sensationalism that often surrounds Bravo’s reality‑TV personalities.

Industry insiders suggest that the public spat could have ramifications for Batula’s career trajectory. Earlier this month, rumors circulated that she was considering an exit from In the City, the New York‑based spin‑off that follows former Summer House cast members as they navigate life in the city. While Bravo has not confirmed any changes to her contract, sources close to the network indicate that the producers are monitoring the situation closely, weighing whether the drama could boost viewership or, conversely, distract from the show’s storyline. Historically, Bravo has leveraged personal conflicts to generate buzz, but the network also remains cautious about alienating audiences with overly toxic narratives.

The incident also shines a light on the broader challenges faced by reality‑TV stars when personal relationships become public property. Cooke, who has been a regular fixture on Summer House since its inception, has a history of confrontational behavior on camera, often blurring the line between scripted tension and genuine animosity. His decision to air grievances on a public platform rather than addressing them privately suggests an attempt to influence public perception, possibly as a strategic move to retain relevance in the competitive reality‑TV market. For Wilson, a relative newcomer to the Bravo ecosystem, the allegations could jeopardize his budding media profile, especially if sponsors or future casting directors view the controversy as a liability.

Looking ahead, Batula’s focus on positivity may prove advantageous both personally and professionally. By refusing to engage in a public war of words, she positions herself as a mature voice amid the chaos, a stance that could resonate with viewers fatigued by relentless drama. Moreover, her willingness to stand by Wilson may solidify their relationship in the eyes of fans, potentially translating into stronger support for any joint ventures they pursue. As the summer season progresses and new episodes of In the City air, audiences will be watching to see whether the couple’s narrative remains a footnote or evolves into a central storyline that could redefine Batula’s place in the Bravo universe.
